faq.q: What is the best stone for skimming?
faq.a: A flat, smooth, roundish stone about the size of your palm and not too heavy. Its flat face gives a big surface for the water to push on.
asks: How do I pick a skimming stone?

faq.q: Why does spin help a skimming stone?
faq.a: Spin keeps the stone steady, the way spin keeps a frisbee stable in the air. Without it the stone would tip, catch its edge and sink at the first touch.
asks: Why flick your wrist when skimming?

faq.q: What angle is best for skimming stones?
faq.a: Experiments published in 2004 found the best tilt is about 20 degrees between the stone and the water's surface. Much steeper or flatter, and the stone loses too much energy at each bounce.
asks: How should the stone hit the water?

faq.q: What is the world record for skimming stones?
faq.a: Kurt Steiner of the United States set the Guinness World Record of 88 skips in 2013, on a river in Pennsylvania.
asks: How many times can a stone skip?

faq.q: Why does the stone eventually sink?
faq.a: Each bounce costs energy through splashing and drag, so the stone slows down. Once it is too slow, the water's upward push can no longer lift it, and it sinks.
asks: Why does a skimming stone stop skipping?

facts: A 2004 study in the journal Nature found the ideal angle between a skimming stone and the water is about 20 degrees.
The Guinness World Record for stone skimming is 88 skips, set by Kurt Steiner in 2013.

quiz.say: Why do good stone skimmers make the stone spin?

options.show: Keeps it level so it doesn't flip and sink
options.say: Keeps it level so it doesn't flip and sink

quiz.why: Spin steadies the stone, so it meets the water flat at a good angle instead of tipping onto its edge.

wrong.0: Spinning doesn't change a stone's weight.
wrong.1: The stone touches the water too briefly to warm it; spin is about steadiness.
